reader.requirement: ACCEPT identifier-2 FROM DAY must deliver YYDDD (year of century, day of year; 25 December 1986 = 86359) as if from an unsigned five-digit integer item, stored by the MOVE rules.

edition-consulted.switches: refuses DATE YYYYMMDD / DAY YYYYDDD (accept-four-digit-year-2002, COBOL0815) and END-ACCEPT (end-accept-2002, COBOL0816) below 2002; the bare DATE / DAY / DAY-OF-WEEK / TIME forms pass through unchanged
the rows accept-four-digit-year-2002 and end-accept-2002 (introduced 2002) that the pass checks
DATE, DAY, DAY-OF-WEEK and TIME are reserved at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023 alike, so a user item of those names is refused (COBOL0901)

reader.edition-search: grep for Edition|CobolVersion|Dialect|Construct in AcceptDisplayBinder.cs, AcceptDisplayEmitter.cs, BoundAccept.cs, AcceptSource.cs and MoveTable16.cs: the binder's ctx.Edition is only the diagnostic sink; the emitter, the conceptual-digit table and the runtime clock reads consult no edition
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: at 2002 and later DAY YYYYDDD exists too; bare DAY is the same five digits, and the YYYYDDD phrase is refused at 85
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f12_01 checks five digits and the ordinal day on the run day; day 366 of a leap year, day 001 of year 00, and edited or group receivers are not exercised

probes.expected: day of year 366 in a leap year, 001 on 1 January with zeros kept
edited with B insertion; truncated on the right into X(2)
receiving ODO group at maximum length 6 (§1985:VI.5.8.4 GR3b)

reader.notes: AcceptSource.Day computes Year mod 100 * 1000 + DayOfYear and the conceptual item is five digits. The pinned runs print the rule's example 86359 and the leap-year and year-00 edges correctly; the witness g85_f12_01 MATCHES at 85.

refuter.evidence: AcceptSource.Day = Year%100*1000+DayOfYear; racc1.cob at 85 pinned 1986-12-25: 9 COMP FROM DAY = 9, XBXBX = [8 6 3], ***,**9 = *86,359, table elements W-E(3) and W-E(4) = 86359. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.5.4 GR8 ["would be expressed as 86359"].
